articles.title: Bridging spatial scales in respiratory viral infection
articles.titleEn: Bridging spatial scales in respiratory viral infection
articles.abstract: Respiratory viruses spread within the host through a combination of local expansion and occasional long-range dissemination that seeds new infection foci. We present LEAP (Lotka-Euler Airway Pathogen model), an analytically tractable within-host model that captures this two-scale process. The model takes the form of an age-dependent branching process and yields a closed-form expression for the exponential growth rate during early infection. Using empirical data to parameterize the model, we find that productive dissemination requires only a small number of successful long-range seeding events per infected cell, with distinct values for SARS-CoV-2 and influenza A virus. LEAP further predicts that, in these well-adapted viruses, interferon-mediated restriction only weakly affects exponential growth, while remaining decisive for poorly adapted pathogens. More broadly, the model provides a flexible framework for experimentally testable predictions of early infection dynamics.

articles.title: Gut microbiota vesicle reprogramming by Ganoderma lucidum polysaccharide alleviates mycoplasmal pneumonia via the gut–lung axis
articles.titleEn: Gut microbiota vesicle reprogramming by Ganoderma lucidum polysaccharide alleviates mycoplasmal pneumonia via the gut–lung axis
articles.abstract: Respiratory infections remain a major global health challenge, further compounded by antibiotic resistance. Among these, mycoplasmal pneumonia represents a particularly prevalent and refractory form. Here, using targeted enzymatic fragmentation combined with multidimensional NMR analysis, we resolved the structure of a homogeneous Ganoderma lucidum polysaccharide, GLFP2, and identified β-(1→6)-linked galactosyl motifs as key structural features. Despite minimal systemic absorption, oral GLFP2 alleviated mycoplasmal pneumonia in mice. Instead, GLFP2 reshaped the gut microbiota and functionally reprogrammed gut microbiota-derived extracellular vesicles (GMEVs), whose transplantation alone was sufficient to confer pulmonary protection. Orally administered GMEVs remained bioactive, showed systemic exposure, associated with the lung, and were preferentially taken up by alveolar macrophages. These vesicles activated AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK) signaling, suppressed the S100A8/A9 inflammatory axis, and limited neutrophil-driven immunopathology. Collectively, these findings identify microbiota-derived vesicles as effectors of gut–lung communication and use a defined polysaccharide to uncover a remote protective mechanism against pneumonia.

articles.title: First-principles channel model and capacity-achieving transmission scheme in thermal noise backscatter links
articles.titleEn: First-principles channel model and capacity-achieving transmission scheme in thermal noise backscatter links
articles.abstract: Thermal noise communication systems transmit information by modulating thermal radiation, eliminating the need for a dedicated signal power source and making them attractive solutions for low-power sensor networks. Their efficiency enables long-lived, unobtrusive operation, which is valuable in the Internet of Things, electromagnetic interference-sensitive environments, and radio frequency identification tag systems. However, a limited understanding of the wireless channel model and efficient transmission schemes has hindered their practical deployment. Here, we present a wireless channel model that elucidates how systems operating at ambient temperature can modulate thermal noise to convey information. Our results reveal a thermal noise backscatter mechanism that enables significantly higher data rates than previously achieved. We designed and built a thermal noise communication system leveraging this mechanism to achieve data rates in the kilobits-per-second range—over two orders of magnitude higher than prior demonstrations. We also derive the system capacity and show that using polar codes, we are able to achieve this expected capacity. Our channel model and transmission scheme pave the way for strategies in thermal noise sensing and communication, advancing practical low-power networking for next-generation wireless applications.

articles.title: Diminishing cooling returns of urban greening amid a warming climate
articles.titleEn: Diminishing cooling returns of urban greening amid a warming climate
articles.abstract: Urban greening is widely prioritized as a nature-based solution to mitigating intensifying heat extremes in the context of climate change, yet its long-term global efficacy remains inadequately quantified. Here we present a two-decade assessment of vegetation dynamics and associated cooling effects across 3,806 urban clusters worldwide, integrating multisource satellite observations with ground measurements from 4,855 meteorological stations. We identify a pronounced climate equity gap: While cities in the Global North have largely expanded green infrastructure, they exhibit cooling saturation with diminishing biophysical returns. Conversely, most cities in the Global South show vegetation stagnation or loss, compounding rapid warming trends. This asymmetry exposes a critical climate justice challenge, indicating that current greening efforts are insufficient to offset a warming trend. Our findings underscore the necessity for context-specific, integrated climate adaptation frameworks that address both the quantity and quality of urban vegetation to achieve equitable thermal resilience in an increasingly warm world.

articles.title: PLD1-driven oncogenic secretion creates a therapeutic vulnerability in chromosome 3q–amplified NSCLC
articles.titleEn: PLD1-driven oncogenic secretion creates a therapeutic vulnerability in chromosome 3q–amplified NSCLC
articles.abstract: Chromosome 3q (3q) amplification is a frequent event in non–small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) and other cancer types, yet therapeutic strategies targeting oncogenic drivers within this amplicon have been unsuccessful. Our study revealed that the 3q amplicon encodes multiple Golgi-related proteins, including Phospholipase D1 (PLD1), which catalyzes the production of a potential oncogenic lipid, phosphatidic acid. We found that PLD1 is highly expressed in 3q-amplified NSCLC (3q-NSCLC) and its enzymatic activity is further boosted by coamplified PLD1 activator, ARF-like GTPase 14. High PLD1 activity is essential for 3q-NSCLC growth and metastasis. Mechanistically, PLD1 drives secretion of oncogenic factors via the carriers from the trans Golgi network to the cell surface pathway to support tumor growth. Transferrin receptor 1 (TFRC), which encodes a membrane protein, is coamplified with PLD1 and overexpressed in 3q-NSCLC. A TFRC antibody–drug conjugate (ADC) carrying a PLD1 inhibitor exhibited potential antitumor activity in mouse models. These findings establish PLD1 as a promoter of 3q-NSCLC and provide proof of concept for the development of PLD1-targeted therapies, including ADC-based approaches, for this challenging cancer subtype.

articles.title: Causality in liquid water as a hallmark of emergent glassy dynamics
articles.titleEn: Causality in liquid water as a hallmark of emergent glassy dynamics
articles.abstract: In molecular liquids such as water, time-delayed influences between microscopic or mesoscopic variables are typically probed using time-correlation functions, which are symmetric under detailed balance and therefore blind to dynamical asymmetries. Here, we characterize water’s dynamics using a causal inference metric that captures asymmetric couplings between collective variables. Analyzing equilibrium molecular dynamics simulations at ambient conditions and in the high-density liquid (HDL) regime of supercooled water, we uncover pronounced asymmetries in the couplings between orientational and translational degrees of freedom across multiple time and length scales. At room temperature, rotational modes exert a modest directional influence on translational dynamics. In contrast, in the supercooled HDL regime, translational motions emerge as the primary drivers of the dynamics, suggesting facilitation-like relaxation mechanisms characteristic of glassy systems. These results reveal a qualitative reorganization of dynamical couplings across thermodynamic conditions, implying that molecular liquids at thermal equilibrium can exhibit an emergent directionality in their fluctuation couplings. As a consequence, our analysis reveals that external perturbations acting on specific degrees of freedom can induce a stronger arrow of time in the causal relations between translational and orientational modes.

articles.title: Heterogeneous amyloid β dimerization revealed by single-molecule FRET and MD simulation
articles.titleEn: Heterogeneous amyloid β dimerization revealed by single-molecule FRET and MD simulation
articles.abstract: The correlation between specific amyloid fibril polymorphs and diseases suggests that characterization of heterogeneity in the aggregation process is key to understanding disease mechanisms. In this work, we use single-molecule Förster resonance energy transfer (FRET) spectroscopy and molecular dynamics (MD) simulation to quantitatively characterize dimerization of amyloid β (Aβ), the first step of the aggregation process. We find that dimerization is extremely rare, with a high dissociation constant of >16 mM, yet there are multiple dimer states with distinct FRET efficiencies and stabilities, many of which survive for milliseconds to seconds. The dimer population increases with the increasing ionic strength and decreasing pH, indicating the importance of nonspecific electrostatic interactions in dimer formation. MD simulations with enhanced sampling demonstrate the formation of diverse bound states having a range of FRET efficiencies and flexible N termini, compatible with the experimental observations. There are conformational clusters represented by the formation of three mixed parallel/antiparallel β strands forming Greek key-like motifs and the formation of antiparallel β strands, which may be representative of dimers with longer and shorter lifetimes, respectively, observed in the FRET experiment. This structural and kinetic heterogeneity, resulting from transient interactions, reflects the rugged energy landscape of amyloid formation and may be related to the great diversity of fibrils ultimately formed in the aggregation process.

articles.title: Disentangling the evolving effects of climate change and technology diffusion on building electricity demand
articles.titleEn: Disentangling the evolving effects of climate change and technology diffusion on building electricity demand
articles.abstract: Climate change and technology diffusion will jointly drive future growth in building electricity demand. How this nonadditive response evolves over time with the pace of climate change and technology diffusion has not previously been examined, despite its importance for maintaining reliable power systems. We estimate electricity demand from residential and commercial buildings under climate change and/or technology diffusion across 183 counties in the United States through 2060. Our framework drives 209,352 machine learning models of building electricity demand with 100 spatiotemporally downscaled climate realizations across four climate models and three emissions scenarios, and 18 technology diffusion pathways of air source heat pumps and insulation. We find that the combined response of peak demand to climate change and technology diffusion diverges substantially from the sum of their individual responses, with distinct patterns across hot and cold grid regions. In cold regions, climate change and technology diffusion drive roughly up to 10 times larger peak demand growth than climate change alone by 2060. Conversely, in hot regions, technology diffusion counteracts climate-change-driven peak demand growth. Across regions, climate-change-induced warming reduces or eliminates a shift toward winter peaking driven by technology diffusion. Via uncertainty partitioning, we find climate-related uncertainty dominates near-term peak demand uncertainty, while technology-diffusion-related uncertainty increases to 10 to 80% of uncertainty by 2060. Internal variability accounts for a much larger share of climate-related uncertainty in peak demand than in temperature itself. Our results demonstrate that capturing nonadditive responses between climate change and technology diffusion is important for planning reliable power systems.

articles.title: Meta-analysis of 990 EBV genomes identifies EBER2 SNP7048 and its interaction with HLA-A*11:01 driving nasopharyngeal carcinoma risk
articles.titleEn: Meta-analysis of 990 EBV genomes identifies EBER2 SNP7048 and its interaction with HLA-A*11:01 driving nasopharyngeal carcinoma risk
articles.abstract: Nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC) is a major health burden in East and Southeast Asia (SEA). While EBV infection is a primary driver, the specific viral strains responsible for NPC development and their interaction with host genetics across geographically diverse endemic regions remain poorly understood. We performed a whole-genome sequencing of 388 EBV isolates and matched host whole-exome sequencing in a Singaporean cohort. To define the global significance of these findings, we conducted a meta-GWAS and phylogenetic analysis across three independent cohorts (Singapore, Hong Kong, and Guangdong and Guangxi provinces of China), totaling 990 EBV genomes. Our study identifies high-risk EBV strains—carrying a core variant in the EBER2 locus (SNP7048)—as the key viral determinator of NPC risk, accounting for approximately 68% of the attributable risk in SEA. Meta-analysis reveals these strains are consistently associated with NPC across all populations, resolving previous regional genetic discordances. We demonstrate a potent synergistic interaction between these EBV risk strains and the host HLA-A*11:01 protective allele; individuals lacking this protection while carrying a high-risk strain exhibit a 30.9-fold increase in NPC risk. Phylogenetic analysis further reveals that these high-risk lineages populated SEA through clonal expansion from Southern China, following historical migration routes. These findings establish that NPC development is driven by the distribution of specific high-risk EBV lineages and their synergistic interaction with host immune susceptibility. This provides a definitive genetic framework for precision population screening and early diagnosis of NPC in the endemic regions.

articles.title: Mechanism of HIV-1 capsid rupture and uncoating by reverse transcription
articles.titleEn: Mechanism of HIV-1 capsid rupture and uncoating by reverse transcription
articles.abstract: One of the key events in the HIV-1 life cycle is reverse transcription (RT), during which single-stranded viral RNA (ssRNA) is converted into double-stranded DNA (dsDNA). This process occurs inside the mature HIV-1 capsid and, once it reaches a critical threshold, drives capsid rupture. This uncoating is essential for infection because it releases viral genetic material into the host cell nucleus. Despite its importance, many mechanistic details of this process remain to be fully understood. To address this gap, we develop a multiscale computational method for simulating RT inside the capsid, termed Coarse-Grained Kinetic Monte Carlo (CG-KMC). CG-KMC stochastically adds deoxynucleotide triphosphates (dNTPs) to the coarse-grained RNA model, enabling stepwise growth of DNA inside the HIV-1 capsid. We implement this method within an integrative coarse-grained framework that combines a “bottom-up” capsid model with a “top-down” representation of the viral RNA/DNA genome. Our simulations phenomenologically capture and predict diverse capsid rupture pathways during RT. The resulting ruptured structures closely match previously identified cryo-ET images. We further perform an extensive analysis of the rupture process, examining its mechanistic and kinetic aspects as well as the role of capsid–DNA interactions. Our findings illuminate how different capsid–DNA conditions give rise to distinct rupture pathways, which differ from ruptures due to simple outward pressure expansion models from within the capsid.

articles.title: Probable Maximum Precipitation: The Smethport Challenge
articles.titleEn: Probable Maximum Precipitation: The Smethport Challenge
articles.abstract: The 18 July 1942 Smethport, Pennsylvania storm produced US and world record rainfall accumulations of 165 mm in 10 min, 240 mm in 25 min and 780 mm in 270 min. Observations from the Smethport storm control sub‐daily Probable Maximum Precipitation (PMP) estimates over a large region of the eastern US. The 18 July 1942 storm is the archetypal example of a Smethport‐Like storm. A prominent feature of Smethport‐Like storms is that they are Northwest Flow events, a class of storm systems linked to development of the summer ridge over the US. The Northwest Flow setting for these storms results in characteristic properties of space‐time variability of rainfall extremes. Polarimetric radar analyses for recent Smethport‐Like storms illustrate the evolution of mesoscale convective systems producing extreme rainfall and provide insights into physical processes associated with peak rainfall rates from the Smethport storm. Smethport‐Like storms are on the extreme high end of the convective intensity spectrum, with storm rotation often contributing to large, intense updrafts. Synoptic scale, mesoscale and storm‐scale properties of Smethport‐Like storms combine to create a near‐optimal environment for extremes of water vapor convergence, a principal ingredient of record, short‐duration rainfall. The central element of the Smethport Challenge is to accurately simulate the climatology of rainfall extremes for Smethport‐Like storms using convection‐permitting climate models.

articles.title: Mechanisms of Ultrasound‐Assisted In Situ Chemical Oxidation for Groundwater Remediation: A Laboratory‐Scale Column Study
articles.titleEn: Mechanisms of Ultrasound‐Assisted In Situ Chemical Oxidation for Groundwater Remediation: A Laboratory‐Scale Column Study
articles.abstract: Groundwater contamination has become an increasingly critical environmental concern worldwide. In situ chemical oxidation (ISCO) is considered a promising technology for groundwater remediation, but its performance in heterogeneous aquifers is often constrained by mass‐transfer limitations in low‐permeability zones, leading to suboptimal treatment efficiency. Theoretically, ultrasound (US) can enhance permeability in low‐permeability regions, accelerate oxidant transport, and activate oxidants to strengthen their degradation capacity; however, the remediation performance and underlying mechanisms of US‐ISCO coupling have not yet been systematically validated through experiments. To address this gap, this study conducted laboratory‐scale packed‐column degradation experiments under three ultrasonic modes (no US, ultrasonic pre‐treatment, and continuous US) and employed nuclear magnetic resonance to characterize the temporal evolution of OTC‐related hydrogen‐bearing signals and pore‐structure changes. The results show that ultrasonic pretreatment modifies the pore structure of the porous medium through cavitation‐ and vibration‐related mechanical effects, thereby enhancing permeability and oxidant mass transfer and consequently accelerating contaminant removal. When US is continuously applied during ISCO, it further intensifies oxidation through thermal and other US‐associated effects. The measured temperature rise promotes oxidation kinetics and mass transfer, while sustained US alters the transformation pathways of several key intermediates, indicating additional reaction routes. These coupled effects yield the highest degradation efficiency through permeability enhancement and in‐reaction US intensification. This study demonstrates the potential of US‐ISCO coupling to improve contaminant removal in low‐permeability porous media and provides a mechanistic basis for its further scale‐up and evaluation under complex hydrogeological conditions.

articles.title: Climate change impacts on groundwater simulated using the AquiFR modelling platform
articles.titleEn: Climate change impacts on groundwater simulated using the AquiFR modelling platform
articles.abstract: In the context of increasing water stress and climate change, the assessment of changes in groundwater resources has become a major challenge for water decision-makers. As part of the EXPLORE2 project, this study aims to estimate changes in groundwater levels on French aquifers during the 21st century. We use the hydrogeological modelling platform AquiFR, forced by 36 regional climate projections from Eurocordex (CMIP5), bias-corrected according to a state-of-the-art method, based on three Representative Concentration Pathways (RCPs): RCP2.6, RCP4.5 and RCP8.5. To better reflect uncertainties, four storylines based on the RCP8.5 scenario have been selected to represent possible futures that illustrate the impacts of worst-case scenarios, to help decision-makers to adopt sustainable groundwater management policies. The future evolution of groundwater is assessed using the standardized piezometric level index, a normalized indicator of groundwater level that provides return periods based on the distribution value over a reference period – in this case 1975–2004. The analyses revealed significant variability between regional climate models. The predominant signal is an increase in groundwater levels, affecting most of the study area, particularly in northern France. This result is in contrast to previous studies in this area. Under the RCP8.5 (highest greenhouse gas emissions scenario), the evolution of the occurrence of current 10-year return period events shows a significant increase in the risk of high groundwater levels, primarily on the northern part of France, which is consistent with 3 out of the 4 storylines. This is accompanied by an increase in the 10-year low groundwater levels mostly observed in the southern part of the French aquifer systems represented by AquiFR. This pattern is shared by all four storylines. This finding underscores a discernible North-South distinction. The increase in the severity of events is a well-known consequence of climate change on surface hydrology, but is less prevalent in groundwater hydrology, which is characterised by a longer residence time.

We use the hydrogeological modelling platform AquiFR, forced by 36 regional climate projections from Eurocordex (CMIP5), bias-corrected according to a state-of-the-art method, based on three Representative Concentration Pathways (RCPs): RCP2.6, RCP4.5 and RCP8.5. To better reflect uncertainties, four storylines based on the RCP8.5 scenario have been selected to represent possible futures that illustrate the impacts of worst-case scenarios, to help decision-makers to adopt sustainable groundwater management policies. The future evolution of groundwater is assessed using the standardized piezometric level index, a normalized indicator of groundwater level that provides return periods based on the distribution value over a reference period – in this case 1975–2004. The analyses revealed significant variability between regional climate models. The predominant signal is an increase in groundwater levels, affecting most of the study area, particularly in northern France. This result is in contrast to previous studies in this area. Under the RCP8.5 (highest greenhouse gas emissions scenario), the evolution of the occurrence of current 10-year return period events shows a significant increase in the risk of high groundwater levels, primarily on the northern part of France, which is consistent with 3 out of the 4 storylines. This is accompanied by an increase in the 10-year low groundwater levels mostly observed in the southern part of the French aquifer systems represented by AquiFR. This pattern is shared by all four storylines. This finding underscores a discernible North-South distinction. The increase in the severity of events is a well-known consequence of climate change on surface hydrology, but is less prevalent in groundwater hydrology, which is characterised by a longer residence time.

articles.title: A Lagrangian particle tracking framework for the super-droplet method in SCALE-SDM 5.2.6-2.3.1: implementation and computational evaluation
articles.titleEn: A Lagrangian particle tracking framework for the super-droplet method in SCALE-SDM 5.2.6-2.3.1: implementation and computational evaluation
articles.abstract: Lagrangian particle histories provide a useful way to diagnose cloud-microphysical pathways in particle-based models, but their practical use in massively parallel super-droplet simulations depends on how particle identifiers, event records, output files, and post-processing workflows are implemented. This paper documents and evaluates a Lagrangian particle-tracking framework in SCALE-SDM 5.2.6-2.3.1. The framework includes forward tracking, backward tracking, and Two-Pass Hybrid Tracking (TPHT). Forward tracking saves the later states of super-droplets selected before or during a simulation. Backward tracking saves the rank and record location of each selected super-droplet's predecessor at the previous output time, so that post-processing can retrieve that record with an 𝒪(1) lookup instead of searching all super-droplets. Both methods use a common procedure to select all valid super-droplets, a random or height–radius-stratified sample, or an externally supplied target list. TPHT uses two integrations over the same physical time interval. The first records super-droplet identifiers when a chosen radius or coalescence condition is met. After duplicate identifiers are removed, the second starts from the same physical and random-number state and writes backward links only for this reduced set. Controlled computational tests are used to characterise runtime, peak random-access memory (RAM), storage (disk-output volume), the effect of output interval on file volume and mean write time, and sampling error and seed-to-seed variability. A three-dimensional DYCOMS-II RF02 stratocumulus case demonstrates TPHT. In this demonstration, the target criteria selected 19.3 % of the estimated valid super-droplet identities, corresponding to an estimated 5.2-fold reduction in retained backward output after temporary identifier files were removed. This factor is specific to the broad criteria used in this test; much larger reductions are possible for problems with sparser target populations. Agreement of the recorded coalescence events between the two integrations provided evidence of reproducibility under the tested configuration. The case study shows that TPHT can identify particles of interest and reconstruct their saved histories while reducing retained output. In future, the same approach could be applied to other history- or event-based questions, including entrainment and mixing, sedimentation, and ice-particle growth.

articles.title: Benchmarking conditioners in Liang–Kleeman Information Flow: application to land–atmosphere interactions in humid forests
articles.titleEn: Benchmarking conditioners in Liang–Kleeman Information Flow: application to land–atmosphere interactions in humid forests
articles.abstract: The Liang–Kleeman Information Flow (LKIF) framework has been increasingly used to identify causality in Earth–system dynamics in recent years. Yet, uncertainties remain regarding how the causal graph changes when mediators and confounders (conditioners) are introduced, i.e., divergence between the bivariate and conditioned forms. A controlled synthetic experiment shows that LKIF preserves correct causal directions under hidden confounding, while differences between bivariate and multivariate estimates still occur. We characterize these differences using time-varying LKIF and introduce several quantifiers, including Conditioner Dominance Index, Moderation Gain, Conditioning Pressure, and Convergence Rate, to evaluate the contributions of conditioners. This is illustrated in an application to soil moisture (SM) and vapor pressure deficit (VPD) couplings with vegetation (leaf area index (LAI) and gross primary productivity (GPP)) in humid forest regions of Southeast China and the Amazon Basin, using satellite-derived and reanalysis data over 1981–2018. We find that the influence of SM on LAI remains consistently stable and shows little sensitivity to the selected conditioners, whereas its influence on GPP and that of VPD on vegetation exhibit substantial divergence between bivariate and multivariate estimates. This divergence peaks under compound dry–hot conditions, with VPD and temperature emerging as dominant conditioners. These results demonstrate that bivariate and multivariate LKIF can yield markedly different conclusions across time and space, especially under compound environmental stress. More importantly, even for the same variables in a causal graph, the same conditioners can affect the temporal evolution of the causal relationships very differently at different locations. This highlights how stationary assumptions may oversimplify causal structure by masking relevant temporal transitions, particularly under compound environmental stress.

articles.title: A review of Last Interglacial sea-level proxies in South Asia and the Indian Ocean
articles.titleEn: A review of Last Interglacial sea-level proxies in South Asia and the Indian Ocean
articles.abstract: In this work, we present a standardized database of Last Interglacial (LIG, ∼132–80 ka) sea-level proxies across the South Asian and Indian Ocean region, including the coasts of Iran, Oman, India, the Maldives, and the Cocos (Keeling) Islands. The database stems from a systematic review of the data included in 17 peer-reviewed studies, structured according to the World Atlas of Last Interglacial Shorelines (WALIS), and is available as Ali et al. (2026, https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.18512769). Within this framework, a total of 54 sea-level index points were re-evaluated to recalculate paleo-RSL elevation and associated uncertainties. This was achieved through updated determinations of their indicative meaning (i.e., reference water level and indicative range), considering the original stratigraphic context, elevation measurement techniques, depositional environments, and chronological constraints. The chronological framework relies on U-Th, luminescence, electron spin resonance, and cosmogenic nuclide dating. These data are characterized by regional differences in the elevation of past relative sea-level proxies that are driven primarily by tectonics, dynamic topography, and glacio-hydro-isostatic forcings. On the active margins of southern Iran and northern Oman, marine terraces dated to Marine Isotope Stage (MIS) 5e (∼125 ka), 5c (∼100 ka), and 5a (∼80 ka) are preserved at 20–60 m a.s.l., reflecting uplift linked to the Zagros foreland and Makran subduction system at least since the Last Interglacial. On the coasts of western and southern India, MIS 5e relative sea-level proxies are found at 1–4 m a.s.l., more in line with near-zero vertical land motion. On Indian Ocean islands, such as the Maldives and Cocos (Keeling) Islands, MIS 5e reefs are now submerged at depths of 10–17 m b.s.l., indicating subsidence since the LIG.

articles.title: Anthropogenic Effects on Elementomes Across Organisms, Ecosystems, and the Biosphere
articles.titleEn: Anthropogenic Effects on Elementomes Across Organisms, Ecosystems, and the Biosphere
articles.abstract: The elemental composition of organisms and ecosystems, termed the “elementome,” fundamentally determines biological function and ecosystem processes. These elemental profiles, historically relatively stable over geological timescales, have been profoundly altered by human activity, especially since the Industrial Revolution, giving rise to a novel “human elementome.” The number and amounts of elements used biologically and nonbiologically by humans, We synthesized multidisciplinary evidence demonstrating this critical shift, characterized by pervasive imbalances in the ratios of carbon, nitrogen, and phosphorus driven by extensive anthropogenic inputs, together with the unprecedented mobilization of a wide spectrum of elements, from critical raw materials and fossil fuels to novel technological elements such as rare‐earth metals. This shift in the human elementome is therefore at the root of many of the environmental changes observed today, as it profoundly alters the cycling, distribution, and availability of chemical elements across ecosystems. These elemental perturbations have not acted in isolation but have interacted synergistically with physiological stresses induced by elevated concentrations of CO 2 , warming, and drought, generating complex emergent effects on life. Our findings highlight a rapid transformation of the fundamental elemental makeup of the biosphere driven by humans, with cascading ecological consequences for ecosystem function and species composition globally. This elemental perspective offers a robust framework for understanding and predicting ecosystem responses in the Anthropocene, informing strategies for conserving biodiversity and managing ecosystems.

articles.title: Different paths, same destination: similar benthic nitrogen cycling sustained by distinct biogeochemical mechanisms in artificialized coastal systems
articles.titleEn: Different paths, same destination: similar benthic nitrogen cycling sustained by distinct biogeochemical mechanisms in artificialized coastal systems
articles.abstract: Human activities are increasingly affecting coastal ecosystems, with shoreline stabilization structures becoming a prevalent response to sea-level rise and extreme climatic events. While these structures aim to protect coastal communities and infrastructures, their effects on ecosystem functioning, and particularly nitrogen cycling and its removal processes such as denitrification, remain poorly understood. To assess the ecological impacts of breakwater construction, we employed a space-for-time substitution approach to examine changes in sediment biogeochemistry, macrobenthic community structure, and nitrogen cycling in an intertidal salt marsh in the St. Lawrence Estuary, Canada. We measured benthic fluxes, denitrification rates, and macrofaunal assemblages at five locations: two landward of the breakwater (impacted sites), one situated immediately seaward of the breakwater (intermediate site) and two reference sites (one vegetated and one unvegetated outside the breakwater system). Landward sites exhibited finer sediment with higher organic carbon content compared to other sites and supported distinct macrobenthic communities dominated by opportunistic Oligochaetes, while reference sites were dominated by Molluscs and Crustaceans. The intermediate seaward site consistently resembled the unvegetated reference site across all variables measured at both sites, including sediment characteristics, oxygen dynamics and benthic fluxes, thereby showing reference-like conditions. Surprisingly, despite these substantial physical and biological changes, dark total benthic oxygen uptake, nitrate and ammonium benthic fluxes showed no consistent separation among impacted, intermediate, and reference sites, while benthic denitrification rates were comparable among the impacted and reference sites where they were measured. This functional similarity reflects an apparent functional convergence arising from distinct combinations of abiotic and biotic factors, including root-mediated rhizosphere oxygenation, macrofauna-mediated sediment irrigation, and contrasting reliance on internally produced versus water-column nitrate. However, this convergence might not apply to all ecosystem services offered by natural salt marshes and may depend on specific biological communities, emphasizing the importance of careful consideration in coastal management decisions.

articles.title: Hydrologically enhanced machine learning framework for urban flood inundation mapping using multi-sensor remote sensing data: a case study of Mumbai, India
articles.titleEn: Hydrologically enhanced machine learning framework for urban flood inundation mapping using multi-sensor remote sensing data: a case study of Mumbai, India
articles.journal: Natural Hazards and Earth System Sciences
articles.abstract: Mapping urban flooding in rapidly urbanizing coastal megacities remains challenging due to complex terrain conditions, high population density, and the limited availability of reliable ground observations. This study presents a hydrologically enhanced machine-learning framework for automated urban flood inundation mapping by integrating multi-sensor satellite observations within a scalable decision-support system. A comprehensive predictor dataset was generated using Sentinel-1 synthetic aperture radar (SAR), Sentinel-2 optical imagery, Shuttle Radar Topography Mission (SRTM) digital elevation data, and Climate Hazards Group InfraRed Precipitation with Station data (CHIRPS) rainfall products through Google Earth Engine. To explicitly represent hydrologic controls on flood propagation that are often overlooked in purely data-driven approaches, two hydrologically informed predictors were incorporated: the Relative Elevation Model (REM), which characterizes terrain-controlled flood accumulation, and the Rainfall-Normalized Index (RNI), which represents rainfall-conditioned surface wetness. A flood inventory was generated by integrating SAR backscatter change detection, optical water indices, and topographic constraints, resulting in approximately 2.6 × 10 5 flooded pixels across the Mumbai Metropolitan Region during the 2019 monsoon season. A balanced stratified sampling strategy was employed to create representative training and testing datasets for supervised classification. Random Forest, optimized Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), and ensemble models were developed and evaluated using standard classification metrics. The optimized XGBoost model achieved the highest predictive performance, with an overall accuracy of 71.7 % and an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.803, outperforming both the Random Forest and ensemble models. The DeLong test indicated statistically significant differences in AUC for the evaluated hydrologic-predictor ablation comparisons at the 95 % confidence level. Feature ablation analysis further demonstrated the importance of hydrologic-topographic predictors, with REM and RNI contributing an increase of approximately 5 %–6 % in AUC. The inclusion of hydrologic predictors improved model discrimination from approximately 0.66 using SAR-only predictors to approximately 0.80 using the complete predictor framework. The resulting flood maps exhibited spatial patterns that were hydrologically consistent with major drainage networks and low-lying areas across the study region. The proposed framework provides a reproducible, scalable, and hydrologically informed and physically interpretable predictors approach for urban flood inundation mapping and demonstrates considerable potential for operational flood monitoring, hazard assessment, and decision-support applications in data-limited tropical urban environments.

articles.title: Terahertz field-induced giant symmetry modulations in a van der Waals antiferromagnet
articles.titleEn: Terahertz field-induced giant symmetry modulations in a van der Waals antiferromagnet
articles.abstract: Strong-field terahertz (THz) excitations enable dynamic control over electronic, lattice and symmetry degrees of freedom in quantum materials. Here, we uncover pronounced terahertz-induced symmetry modulations and coherent phonon dynamics in the van der Waals antiferromagnet MnPS 3 , in which inversion symmetry is broken by its antiferromagnetic spin configuration. Our time-resolved second harmonic generation measurements reveal long-lived giant oscillations in the antiferromagnetic phase, with amplitudes comparable to the equilibrium signal, driven by phonons involving percent-level atomic displacements relative to the equilibrium bond lengths. The temporal evolution of the rotational anisotropy patterns indicates a dynamic breaking of mirror symmetry, modulated by two vibrational modes at 1.7 THz and 4.5 THz, with the former corresponding to a hidden mode not observed in equilibrium spectroscopy. These effects arise in part from a field-induced charge rearrangement mechanism that lowers the local crystal symmetry and couples to the phonon modes. We uncover a long-lived field-driven response with a complex THz polarization dependence, consistent with a metastable state of reduced symmetry. Through comparison with simulations, we interpret this response in terms of a potential antiferromagnetic-to-ferrimagnetic transition. Our results establish an effective field-tunable pathway for driving excitations otherwise weak in equilibrium.

articles.title: Comprehensive spectroscopic analysis of energy inversion of the lowest singlet and triplet excited states in the heptazine HzTFEX2
articles.titleEn: Comprehensive spectroscopic analysis of energy inversion of the lowest singlet and triplet excited states in the heptazine HzTFEX2
articles.abstract: Detailed photophysical measurements of the non-symmetric heptazine, HzTFEX 2 , previously reported as having inverted S 1 -T 1 levels, show complex behaviour, highly dependent on environment, concentration and aggregation. Here we show that, single crystals of HzTFEX 2 show anti-Kasha S 0 ←S 2 and excimer emission. Solution state absorption shows a hypsochromic shift of the π-π* S 0 →S 1 , linearly dependent on solvent polarizability. In most environments, emission is dominated by excimer species, only in toluene and frozen 2-MeTHF do monomeric properties dominate. In frozen solutions, aggregation phenomena are solvent dependent. Given such complexity, time-dependent emission spectra are crowded, making it difficult to resolve monomeric phosphorescence. However, by exciting S 0 →S 2 at 77 K, we observe a consistent phosphorescence signal at 425 nm, 110 ± 20 meV above the S 0 ←S 1 emission, whereas exciting S 0 →S 1 does not give phosphorescence or delayed fluorescence (DF). We conclude that coupling between S 2 and S 1 is very weak, S 2 -T N intersystem crossing is effective, whereas S 1 ↔T 1 intersystem crossing is thermally activated, fulfilling the conditions required for the observation of inverted phosphorescence. At room temperature, no long-lived DF is observed because exothermic T 1 →S 1 ISC becomes allowed, such that in an OLED, high efficiency can be achieved.

articles.title: Terahertz emission by X-ray difference-frequency generation
articles.titleEn: Terahertz emission by X-ray difference-frequency generation
articles.abstract: Nonlinear interactions between X-rays and matter represent a new frontier in ultrafast science. However, X-ray difference-frequency generation (DFG)—a fundamental second-order nonlinear optical process—has not been experimentally observed until now. Here, we report the first observation of terahertz emission induced by hard X-ray free-electron laser (XFEL) pulses in solids, providing evidence for X-ray DFG. Using 10-fs, 10-keV XFEL pulses incident on ZnTe, we detected terahertz emission arising from wave mixing between different spectral components within the XFEL bandwidth. The emitted terahertz waves originate from second-order nonlinear polarization evolving on a femtosecond timescale. The polarization and angular dependences of the terahertz emission confirm that X-ray DFG is mediated not only by DFG without spatial inversion symmetry but also by DFG with spatial inversion symmetry. Quantitative analysis yields a DFG susceptibility ratio of the former to the latter of 58±4%, and the generation efficiency for 10 keV excitation is approximately 1% of that for near-infrared 1.55 eV excitation in the 100-μm-thick ZnTe crystal, while the intrinsic response normalized by interaction length is comparable. These results establish XFEL-induced terahertz emission as a general platform for probing second-order X-ray nonlinearities and ultrafast polarization dynamics in solids.

articles.title: High-risk antimicrobial resistance genomic traits in multidrug-resistant Salmonella across China’s food chain: projections to 2050
articles.titleEn: High-risk antimicrobial resistance genomic traits in multidrug-resistant Salmonella across China’s food chain: projections to 2050
articles.abstract: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) is rising globally, yet factors shaping its genomic evolution remain poorly understood. We investigated how socioeconomic, climate, and health factors are associated with AMR spread in multi-drug resistant (MDR) Salmonella enterica across China’s food chain, mapped hotspots and forecasted genomic trait prevalence to 2050. We analysed 2,536 MDR genomes from 15 provinces over 16 years, covering patients, food and non-food workers, meat, livestock, and environmental sources. A machine learning framework integrated genomic surveillance with risk assessment to identify high-risk AMR traits (clinically relevant, MDR, mobile). Regression models linked trait prevalence to socioeconomic, climate, health, and antimicrobial consumption data, informing projections to 2050. Eighty-four high-risk traits, including carbapenem, colistin, and β-lactam resistance, are projected to rise, with antibiotic use, population growth, healthcare spending, and urbanisation. Projections were trait-specific: bla CTX-M-64 and bla TEM-1 may increase up to 20%, while bla CTX-M-65 and bla CTX-M-14 remain below 5%. A mechanistic shift in fluoroquinolone resistance is projected: mutation-based resistance ( gyrA 87) declines while plasmid-mediated genes ( qnrB17 , qnrS1 ) rise. Food workers emerged as a potential reservoir, showing higher trait prevalence than food sources, uniquely carrying last-resort antibiotic-resistance genes ( bla TEM-30 , bla NDM-5 , bla CTX-M-64 ). Integrating genomic with socioeconomic surveillance could shift AMR interventions from reactive to preventive.

articles.title: Strong field spectroscopy of many-body interactions in solids
articles.titleEn: Strong field spectroscopy of many-body interactions in solids
articles.abstract: High-order harmonic generation (HHG) in solids offers a promising route to compact ultrafast sources of quantum light, but its efficiency and coherence are limited by ultrafast dephasing of laser-driven electron–hole polarization. Although widely described by a phenomenological coherence time, the microscopic origin of this dephasing has remained unresolved. Here, we combine wavelength-dependent HHG measurements in monolayer and bulk semiconductors with ab initio many-body calculations of electron–phonon scattering and strong-field simulations. We show that the measured wavelength scaling of the HHG yield is quantitatively reproduced only when semiconductor Bloch equations incorporate momentum-dependent dephasing derived from first principles scattering rates. The calculations reveal that strong-field-driven carriers rapidly enter regions of the Brillouin zone with enhanced electron–phonon scattering, giving rise to effective few-femtosecond dephasing. Our results establish a microscopic foundation for dephasing in solid-state HHG and provide a framework for engineering coherence in strongly driven solids for quantum photonic applications.

articles.title: Quantifying the Impacts of Excess Water on Agricultural Losses and the Role of Adaptive Infrastructure
articles.titleEn: Quantifying the Impacts of Excess Water on Agricultural Losses and the Role of Adaptive Infrastructure
articles.abstract: Excess water during the planting season is a growing source of production and income risk for agriculture. Yet its impacts remain poorly quantified. Existing studies typically rely on precipitation‐based indicators and therefore miss how soil saturation, runoff dynamics, and adaptive infrastructure shape crop failure. This paper fills that gap by integrating high‐resolution hydrologic model outputs with county‐level reports of failed and prevented planting across the U.S. Midwest from 2009 to 2020. We construct process‐based measures of runoff and soil moisture and evaluate their ability to explain losses while explicitly accounting for the presence of subsurface drainage systems. Hydrologic indicators strongly predict planting‐season losses: one additional day above the 95th‐percentile runoff threshold was associated with increase in failed or prevented acres by 0.37–0.42 percent. Counties with extensive artificial drainage see up to a 4.38 percent reduction in failed acres (up to 87% reduction in planting risk). Aggregated across the region, subsurface drainage preserved an estimated $13.53 billion in avoided agricultural losses over the study period. The results demonstrate that model‐derived excess‐water metrics outperform precipitation in most model setups. In particular, runoff‐based measures become especially informative when accounting for interactions with subsurface drainage infrastructure, highlighting how hydrologic context shapes crop susceptibility to excess water. The findings show the value of integrating hydrologic processes and adaptive infrastructure into agricultural risk assessment within coupled human–environment systems. Despite the value of drainage demonstrated here, future integrative work must consider potential tradeoffs imposed by nitrate concentrations and export.

articles.title: Impact of Junction Angle on Density‐Driven Secondary Flow and Mixing Rates at River Confluences: A Numerical Investigation
articles.titleEn: Impact of Junction Angle on Density‐Driven Secondary Flow and Mixing Rates at River Confluences: A Numerical Investigation
articles.abstract: It is now well understood that a small difference in the density of two rivers can cause density‐driven streamwise vortices (SOVs) to form and their mixing interface to tilt downstream of their confluence. However, much less knowledge exists pertaining to how these processes are affected by other key confluence parameters such as the discharge ratio and junction angle. This study uses eddy‐resolving simulations of an experimental confluence flume to parametrically investigate how increasing junction angle under a range of and discharge ratios affect flow structure. The findings demonstrate that increasing junction angle increases the width of the mixing interface near the apex as well as mixing rates. However, the contribution of junction angle is shown to be incidental compared to that of . Increasing has an overwhelming effect on the lateral expansion of the mixing interface, the magnitude of streamwise circulation, and ultimately, mixing rates compared to the junction angle. Increasing also increases the tilting of the mixing interface, leading to increased lateral stretching of the vertically oriented Kelvin‐Helmholtz vortices, resulting in a rapid loss in their coherence downstream. The simulations indicate the SOVs decay in the streamwise direction due to interaction with the free surface and the bed. Our use of smooth downstream corners, similar to those present at natural river confluences, suggests that the role of the junction angle has likely been overestimated in previous laboratory and modeling studies, which focused on asymmetrical junctions featuring a sharp downstream corner and a wide separation zone.

articles.title: Basin-scale evaluation of the Noah-MP land surface model for runoff and snow generation in the Missouri River Basin: insights and recommendations for parameterization scheme selection
articles.titleEn: Basin-scale evaluation of the Noah-MP land surface model for runoff and snow generation in the Missouri River Basin: insights and recommendations for parameterization scheme selection
articles.abstract: Process-based land surface models, such as the Noah-Multiparameterization (Noah-MP) model, are widely used for large-scale hydrologic simulations because of their flexibility in selecting multiple parameterization schemes. However, limited guidance on choosing appropriate configurations constrains their reliability in representing runoff and snowmelt dynamics across diverse land-cover and snow conditions. This study evaluates the default and four alternative parameterization schemes in the Noah-MP land surface model, including Runoff and Groundwater (RUN), Surface Exchange Coefficient for Heat (SFC), Frozen Soil Permeability (INF), and Snow/Soil Temperature Time Scheme (STC), across 50 Hydro-Climate Data Networks (HCDNs) in the Missouri River Basin. Model performance was evaluated using USGS streamflow observations and snow water equivalent (SWE) estimates from the University of Arizona dataset for 2014–2023. Results showed that the alternative schemes improved runoff simulation compared to the default scheme through different approaches representing key hydrological and thermodynamic processes. Specifically, the RUN, SFC, INF, and STC experiments improved the Kling–Gupta Efficiency (KGE) by 0.19, 0.38, 0.44, and 0.14, respectively in representative subbasins, through enhanced groundwater dynamics, reduced evapotranspiration bias, improved rapid runoff response, and more accurate SWE evolution. SWE evaluation further indicates that the STC experiment most effectively reduced SWE bias in snow-dominated subbasins, though improvements in SWE did not universally translate into better runoff simulation. These results highlight the importance of basin-specific parameterization schemes within Noah-MP to improve hydrological prediction and water management across diverse hydroclimatic regions. The findings further indicate optimal parameterization schemes for different climates, land cover, and snow regimes.

articles.title: Improving photosynthate allocation dynamic simulations of crops under water stress conditions
articles.titleEn: Improving photosynthate allocation dynamic simulations of crops under water stress conditions
articles.abstract: Accurately simulating crop photosynthate allocation under water stress is critical for predicting both food security and ecosystem carbon inputs. Current crop models often rely on static or growth-stage-fixed allocation coefficients, which limits their ability to capture the physiological plasticity of crops responding to fluctuating environmental conditions. This study develops a water-driven, stage-dependent carbon allocation scheme within the Agro-C model to better represent crop responses to soil moisture variability. The scheme dynamically adjusts photosynthate allocation coefficients for roots (PR) and leaves (PL), integrates the yellow-to-green leaf ratio (YGR), and incorporates a water stress-induced leaf senescence module. By coupling carbon allocation to both soil moisture and crop development, the approach improves the representation of physiologically regulated allocation processes and enhances the realism of crop simulations. Model evaluation using extensive observation datasets for maize and wheat demonstrates substantial improvements in simulation accuracy, with R 2 values reaching 0.77–0.95 for aboveground biomass (AGB) and 0.62–0.83 for belowground biomass (BGB). These results underscore the importance of dynamically representing carbon allocation under water stress and offer an improved framework for simulating carbon–water interactions in agroecosystems.

articles.title: Development and validation of ARMS-gb v2.0: extending fast radiative transfer modeling capability to all-sky conditions for ground-based microwave radiometer retrievals
articles.titleEn: Development and validation of ARMS-gb v2.0: extending fast radiative transfer modeling capability to all-sky conditions for ground-based microwave radiometer retrievals
articles.abstract: Ground-based microwave radiometers provide continuous, all-weather observations of boundary-layer temperature and humidity, closing a critical near-surface observation gap. The Advanced Radiative Transfer Modeling System – ground-based (ARMS-gb) is a fast radiative transfer model specifically designed to simulate the brightness temperatures observed by these instruments. This paper presents ARMS-gb v2.0, which introduces a hydrometeor absorption and scattering module and an accelerated discrete ordinate method (ADOM) solver for multiple scattering. The model now simulates cloud water, rain, ice, snow, and graupel using optical-property look-up tables computed with Mie theory and the discrete dipole approximation (DDA). The existing tangent-linear and adjoint (TL/AD) modules are also extended to include hydrometeor processes, supporting all-sky retrieval and variational data assimilation. Validation against field measurements from 14- and 22-channel ground-based microwave radiometers indicates that ARMS-gb v2.0 effectively simulates brightness temperatures under cloudy non-precipitating conditions, with the mean observed minus simulated brightness temperature generally within 1 K of the corresponding clear-sky baseline. Compared with ARMS-gb v1.0, which neglects cloud effects, the root mean square error (RMSE) under cloudy conditions decreases by 1–2 K in the water-vapor band, most notably at 30 GHz, where the coefficient of determination ( R 2 ) increases from 0.55 to 0.77. In the weak oxygen band, where frozen hydrometeors have stronger scattering effects, the observation-minus-background (O–B) decreases by 3–4 K. At 51 GHz, the RMSE decreases from 5.23 to 3.22 K, and R 2 increases from 0.52 to 0.81. Moreover, the results indicate that the DDA model slightly outperforms the Mie model in characterizing frozen hydrometeors at these channels. However, large O–B departures remain during precipitation events, with RMSE values in the water-vapor absorption band reaching 30–40 K, reflecting rain-contaminated measurement effects and atmospheric hydrometeor uncertainties that require dedicated quality control and observation-error modeling before assimilation or retrieval applications.

articles.title: High-resolution global groundwater storage anomalies: a 1 km downscaled dataset
articles.titleEn: High-resolution global groundwater storage anomalies: a 1 km downscaled dataset
articles.abstract: Groundwater depletion poses a challenge to water security, but the coarse spatial resolution of Gravity Recovery and Climate Experiment (GRACE) observations limits the characterization of groundwater variability at regional and local scales. Here, we present a 1 km monthly global groundwater storage anomaly (GWSA) dataset covering April 2002–December 2020. The dataset was generated using Singular Spectrum Analysis (SSA) for temporal gap filling, 19 high-resolution hydroclimatic and geophysical predictors, and aquifer-stratified machine-learning downscaling. Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) and deep neural networks (DNN) were evaluated as candidate models, and XGBoost was selected for dataset production based on internal, cross-scale, and in-situ evaluations. When aggregated to the original GRACE scale, the 1 km product agreed closely with the original GWSA ( R 2 = 0.972, RMSE = 2.10 cm). Independent evaluation used a global archive of 152 069 groundwater-monitoring wells and a 1° spatial-block calibration–validation design. Effective specific yield ( S yeff ) was estimated from calibration blocks and transferred to held-out blocks before comparison at a common 0.25° grid. For XGBoost, the held-out evaluation yielded R 2 = 0.538, RMSE = 0.378 cm yr −1 , and Bias = 0.106 cm yr −1 . The association between modeled and observation-derived trends remained similar under ± 30 % perturbations in S yeff , although amplitude-related metrics were more sensitive to the conversion coefficient. Standardized time-series comparisons and monthly evaluations of representative aquifers showed better agreement for long-term variability than for seasonal variability. Comparisons with published regional estimates showed close agreement in the North China Plain, weaker depletion magnitudes in northwestern India and California, and a trend-sign mismatch in the High Plains Aquifer during 2003–2013. Experiments using CSR, JPL, H08, and WaterGAP also showed that reconstruction performance and predictor importance depend on the target product. The dataset provides kilometre-scale estimates of groundwater-storage variability under the large-scale GRACE constraint. Local interpretation of the reconstructed spatial patterns requires additional groundwater-level, abstraction, and hydrogeological observations. The 1 km monthly global GWSA dataset is openly available from the National Cryosphere Desert Data Center at https://doi.org/10.12072/ncdc.hydrology.db7323.2026 (Fan et al., 2026).

articles.title: TED: a global temperature-driven thermoelastic displacement dataset for GNSS reference stations (2000–2023)
articles.titleEn: TED: a global temperature-driven thermoelastic displacement dataset for GNSS reference stations (2000–2023)
articles.abstract: Nonlinear variations in GNSS station height time series include contributions from non-tidal mass loading and temperature-driven thermoelastic displacement (TED). However, a globally consistent station-level TED product has not been widely available. Here we present a global dataset of vertical TED for approximately 14 000 GNSS stations over 2000–2023, generated using a full-spectrum layered finite-element model. The model is driven by hourly ERA5 soil-temperature forcing and parameterized with SoilGrids-derived depth-dependent subsurface properties, allowing within-day temperature variability to be incorporated into daily TED time series that retain seasonal and nonseasonal components. For the 2612 stations with documented foundation-depth information, site-information-constrained solutions agree closely with SoilGrids-based solutions, with annual-amplitude differences mostly about 0.01–0.03 mm and annual-phase differences generally within 1–3°. Sensitivity tests using ± 10 % perturbations in the linear thermal expansion coefficient, thermal diffusivity, and Young's modulus indicate that the amplitude and phase of the annual TED component are stable under reasonable parameter uncertainty. Globally, annual TED amplitudes are mostly within about 0.2–1.2 mm and locally exceed 1.5 mm, with larger signals concentrated in arid inland and continental regions. The percentile-based peak-to-peak variability of the full daily TED series commonly reaches 2–4 mm and locally approaches 5–6 mm. When applied alone to GNSS height time series, TED produces positive WRMS reductions at about 79 % of the assessed stations, with most improvements within 3 %–5 % and the largest reductions reaching about 10 %. The dataset is publicly available for direct use in GNSS height time series correction and related geophysical applications: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21069958 (Lu et al., 2026a).

articles.title: Carbon Accumulation in Tropical Dry Forests and Savannas Despite Widespread Land‐Cover Change, Revealed by Radar Remote Sensing
articles.titleEn: Carbon Accumulation in Tropical Dry Forests and Savannas Despite Widespread Land‐Cover Change, Revealed by Radar Remote Sensing
articles.abstract: Accurate mapping of woody biomass and its temporal change is critical for understanding the global carbon balance, informing restoration and supporting evidence‐based policy on climate mitigation and livelihoods. The vegetation of the dry tropics, comprised largely of dry forests and savannas, holds substantial woody carbon stocks, but both stocks and change over time remain uncertain. Where Earth Observation (EO) data have been used to estimate change over time, different products give conflicting results on the direction, magnitude and location of change. We present pan‐dry‐tropical maps of aboveground carbon density (AGCD) and AGCD change at 100 m resolution for the years 2015–2024, developed using ALOS ScanSAR satellite radar observations calibrated with in situ measurements ( n = 237). These maps suggest an aboveground woody carbon pool (AGC) in the dry tropics of 25.3 2.0 PgC, ~13.0% of global AGC. Net AGC has increased by 0.43 0.07 PgC yr −1 , ~20.0% of the global net land sink. The overall net increase (0.43 PgC yr −1 ) is comprised of gross losses from deforestation and degradation (0.27 0.05 PgC yr −1 ) and gains due to densification and extensification of 0.59 0.1 PgC yr −1 , with the balance accounted for by small changes (change −1 ). Losses are equally split between degradation and deforestation, while gains are divided roughly 2:1 between the densification of woody ecosystems and expansion into previously grass‐dominated areas. These new maps, created with a dry‐tropics‐specific EO method, highlight the importance of tropical dry forests and savannas in the global carbon cycle. The prominent role of degradation‐related losses suggests that climate change mitigation will need to focus much more on reducing losses from overharvesting than at present. The widespread increases in carbon density and the increase in tree biomass into open systems present major challenges for biodiversity conservation, restoration and livelihoods.

articles.title: Thermal Generalism Shapes Tolerance to Extreme Heatwaves in Estuarine Fishes
articles.titleEn: Thermal Generalism Shapes Tolerance to Extreme Heatwaves in Estuarine Fishes
articles.abstract: Climate change is widely expected to push many taxa beyond their biological limits, yet some populations persist in environments that routinely experience climatic extremes. This raises a fundamental question: does their thermal tolerance reflect species‐level thermal generalism (an evolved capacity to maintain performance across a broad thermal range) or population‐specific acclimation to local conditions (phenotypic plasticity)? Distinguishing between these alternatives is key for predicting whether tolerance to climatic extremes will generalise across species distributions or remain restricted to heat‐tolerant populations. To test these competing hypotheses, we quantified physiological performance (at cellular and organismal levels) in three economically important estuarine fish ( Acanthopagrus australis , Sillago ciliata and Rhabdosargus sarba ) collected from 20 sites across 15 estuaries along a ~1000‐km latitudinal gradient spanning their core and poleward range edges. Sites differed in thermal variability, including some that intermittently exceeded the severest end‐of‐century climate projections. We then experimentally exposed two of the fish species from low and high thermal variability sites to moderate (+2°C, 14 days) or extreme (+4°C, 7 days) simulated marine heatwave events, assessing 12 physiological and behavioural proxies. All three species collected in situ maintained comparable physiological performance across sites of contrasting thermal variability. Both experimental species, each collected from a single high‐ and low‐variability site, tolerated heatwave conditions regardless of thermal history or heatwave intensity, supporting species‐level thermal generalism rather than population‐specific acclimation. In the absence of heatwave conditions, S. ciliata from high‐variability sites also showed steeper allometric scaling and faster growth at 26 versus 24°C experimental control temperatures, suggesting this species may benefit from the warmer baseline temperatures projected under gradual climate change. Combined, our findings support thermal generalism as the primary driver of tolerance in estuarine fishes to climatic extremes, with important implications for the fisheries they support under climate change.

articles.title: Linking sea–air and benthic methane fluxes across seasons in a tropical seagrass meadow of Taiwan
articles.titleEn: Linking sea–air and benthic methane fluxes across seasons in a tropical seagrass meadow of Taiwan
articles.abstract: Seagrass meadows are important blue carbon ecosystems that sequester large amounts of organic carbon but can also emit methane (CH 4 ), potentially offsetting part of their climate mitigation benefits. However, the seasonal and diurnal dynamics of CH 4 production and emissions in tropical seagrass ecosystems remain poorly understood. This study presents the first integrated assessment of CH 4 cycling in the Haikou seagrass meadow, southern Taiwan. Field campaigns conducted between May 2022 and June 2023 combined surface water sampling, in situ benthic chamber incubations, and porewater profiling in a Thalassia hemprichii–Halophila pinifolia seagrass meadow to quantify CH 4 dynamics at both the sediment-to-water and sea-to-air interfaces. The seagrass meadow exhibited higher dissolved CH 4 concentrations and sea-to-air CH 4 fluxes than adjacent coastal waters, confirming that it functions as a localized atmospheric CH 4 hotspot. Nighttime dissolved CH 4 concentrations generally exceeded daytime values, reflecting diurnal variations in oxygen availability, whereas seasonal variability in sea-to-air CH 4 fluxes was primarily driven by wind speed. Mean sediment-to-water and sea-to-air CH 4 fluxes were 88.2±41.2 and 4.9±2.2µmol m −2 d −1 , respectively. Despite substantial benthic CH 4 production, atmospheric emissions remained comparatively low, indicating a marked decoupling between sediment-to-water and sea-to-air CH 4 fluxes. This decoupling suggests that much of the sediment-derived CH 4 was transported laterally by tidal exchange and coastal circulation before atmospheric release, with microbial oxidation acting as an additional sink. Compared with adjacent bare sand sediments, seagrass sediments maintained higher baseline CH 4 production rates and benthic fluxes owing to greater organic matter availability and favorable microbial conditions, whereas unvegetated sandy sediments generally exhibited low CH 4 production but produced episodic CH 4 pulses following storm-induced sediment disturbance. Elevated porewater CH 4 concentrations during summer and autumn further indicated enhanced methanogenesis associated with organic matter accumulation under calmer hydrodynamic conditions. Overall, these findings demonstrate that CH 4 cycling in tropical seagrass meadows is jointly regulated by biological processes and hydrodynamic conditions, highlighting the need to consider both CH 4 emissions and carbon sequestration when evaluating the climate benefits of blue carbon ecosystems.

articles.title: Detecting long-term canopy change and vegetation shifts in northern peatlands using LAI and climate data
articles.titleEn: Detecting long-term canopy change and vegetation shifts in northern peatlands using LAI and climate data
articles.abstract: Northern peatlands store vast amounts of carbon, part of which might be released to the atmosphere as climate warming alters peatland canopies. To track these changes, we analysed recent greening and browning across northern peatlands, defined here as increases and decreases in leaf area index (LAI), from 2001 to 2023. We assessed vegetation change using gap-filled, sensor-independent LAI climate data record at 500 m resolution across the peatland-dominated pixels north of 45° N, defined as pixels with at least 90 % mapped peatland cover and no detected wildfire during 2001–2023. To our knowledge, our results provide the first multi-decadal assessment of peatland canopy change based strictly on mapped peatlands rather than on the broader Arctic and boreal domain in which peatlands are usually embedded. Although greening was widespread at the pixel level (77 % of studied peatlands; greening-to-browning ratio 3.5:1), the area-weighted LAI trend at the map scale was not significant. LAI anomalies were weakly positively correlated with air temperature and weakly negatively correlated with precipitation; multi-year mean annual precipitation, rather than air temperature, was retained in the model of long-term LAI trends. Higher tree cover was associated with less greening, but this association was weaker in peatlands with deciduous needleleaf cover and where precipitation was higher. Most peatland pixels showed a linear LAI trend with no breakpoints; where non-linear trends occurred, their breakpoints were often temporally aligned with phase shifts in the Pacific Decadal Oscillation. These non-linear trends differed by region: trends in which LAI first decreased and then increased were concentrated in West Siberia, whereas trends in which LAI first increased and then decreased were widespread across Europe, northeastern Asia, and Canada. Protected peatlands did not show different LAI trends once differences in climate and canopy were accounted for. Overall, recent peatland canopy change was not a uniform increase in greenness but rather reflected moisture-sensitive, tree-composition-dependent responses modulated by decadal climate variability.

articles.title: Application of radar remote sensing for cyclone damage mapping in Bangladesh: a coherence-based approach
articles.titleEn: Application of radar remote sensing for cyclone damage mapping in Bangladesh: a coherence-based approach
articles.journal: Natural Hazards and Earth System Sciences
articles.abstract: Rapid and reliable assessment of cyclone-induced damage remains a major challenge in coastal regions where cloud cover and limited accessibility constrain conventional approaches. This study presents a coherence-based Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) framework for identifying and quantifying cyclone-induced surface changes in the coastal districts of Bangladesh. Multi-temporal Sentinel-1 data were analyzed using interferometric coherence to capture spatial and temporal variations associated with five major cyclones: Amphan (2020), Sitrang (2022), Mocha (2023), Hamoon (2023), and Remal (2024). A time-series approach incorporating multiple pre-, during-, and post-event image pairs was implemented to distinguish cyclone-driven changes from natural surface variability and to improve detection reliability. The results reveal a consistent decline in coherence during cyclone events, followed by gradual recovery. Spatial analysis indicates that areas of significant coherence loss correspond to zones affected by flooding, vegetation damage, and structural disruption. Estimated damage extents varied across cyclones, with Remal (2024) showing the largest affected area (∼ 601 km 2 ), followed by Mocha (∼ 474 km 2 ), Amphan (∼ 288 km 2 ), Sitrang (∼ 122 km 2 ), and Hamoon (∼ 117 km 2 ). Validation using field observations and secondary data yielded an overall classification accuracy of 94 %, confirming the robustness of the coherence-based approach. Complementary inundation mapping further demonstrated that coherence captures a broader spectrum of cyclone impacts beyond flood extent alone, including wind-induced damage and geomorphic changes. This study establishes multi-temporal SAR coherence analysis as a scalable, cloud-independent, and operationally effective tool for rapid post-cyclone damage assessment. The proposed framework enhances the reliability of disaster monitoring in complex coastal environments and offers strong potential for integration into near-real-time disaster response systems. Future research should focus on integrating multi-sensor datasets and long-term coherence time series to refine damage characterization and reduce uncertainty.

articles.title: Closed-loop photoreactor design enabled by machine learning and digital twins
articles.titleEn: Closed-loop photoreactor design enabled by machine learning and digital twins
articles.abstract: Designing efficient photoreactors remains challenging due to the complex interplay of reflection, scattering, and absorption. Here, we introduce a closed-loop workflow integrating ray-tracing digital twins with multi-objective Bayesian optimization to design photoreactors with high photon capture and uniform irradiation. A digital 3D reactor model is calibrated using measured emission characteristics, reflectivity data, and geometrical properties and validated against potassium ferrioxalate actinometry. The validated model explores reflector shape and vial positioning, identifying geometries that maximize incident photon flux while maintaining homogeneity across 16 vials. Experimental validation using a photocatalytic Suzuki–Miyaura cross-coupling shows that reaction yields track simulated photon flux. The optimized reactor is further applied to quantum-yield screening, enabling mechanistic insights across diverse conditions in a single experiment. This work establishes an experimentally validated virtual co-design framework in which machine learning and digital twins accelerate photoreactor development and support quantitative understanding of photochemical processes.

articles.title: Nuclear adaptation to intracellular mechanical forces regulates the phagocytic capacity of Drosophila macrophages in vivo
articles.titleEn: Nuclear adaptation to intracellular mechanical forces regulates the phagocytic capacity of Drosophila macrophages in vivo
articles.abstract: How macrophages fine-tune their appetite to fulfil their clearance role is incompletely understood. Phagocytosis exacerbates cytoplasmic crowding, but whether macrophages can sense this increase and use it to regulate their phagocytic capacity has never been investigated. Here, we test the hypothesis that phagosomes exert a strain on the nucleus, which in turn responds to the intracellular mechanical inputs influencing macrophage appetite. Combining genetic manipulation and live in vivo imaging, we show that engulfed apoptotic bodies indent and deform the nucleus of Drosophila embryonic macrophages, and that phagocytosis increases Lamin B levels. Importantly, we show that silencing Lamin B or components of the LINC complex negatively regulates apoptotic body engulfment in vivo. Thus, we demonstrate that phagosome-induced nuclear molecular and mechanical adaptations are critical for Drosophila embryonic macrophages to sustain apoptotic corpse uptake, thereby unveiling a role for nuclear plasticity in the regulation of macrophage phagocytic capacity in vivo.

articles.title: The 2023 North Atlantic marine heatwave could have evolved into a far more extreme event
articles.titleEn: The 2023 North Atlantic marine heatwave could have evolved into a far more extreme event
articles.abstract: In 2023, the North Atlantic Ocean experienced a marine heatwave of unprecedented intensity and duration, raising the question of whether substantially more severe outcomes were physically plausible under comparable present-day preconditioning, and which processes could produce them. Here, we apply ensemble boosting to a coupled Earth system model to generate physically consistent alternative evolutions of a 2023-like event. The boosted ensemble produced marine heatwaves lasting up to 579 days, reaching maximum intensities of 4.5 °C above climatology and cumulative intensities of 717 °C·days, compared with 240 days, 2.9 °C and 224 °C·days in observations. Detailed analyses of the longest and most intense events highlight contrasting roles for persistent Euro-Atlantic high pressure, reduced turbulent heat loss, enhanced shortwave radiation and upper-ocean heat redistribution. Finally, we place these present-day storylines in the context of future warming, showing that events comparable to the observed 2023 event become increasingly common as global warming progresses.
